scope: Proposition 4.2 (Continuation to the sphere family) of the manuscript “Smooth anisotropic uniqueness in the Calderón problem from one boundary patch” (preprints/Smooth-Anisotropic-Uniqueness-in-the-Calderon-Problem-from-One-Boundary-Patch-September-24-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 365 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 1ec46ed64206d12d), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 22. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Choose p sufficiently large and then ε > 0 sufficiently small in terms of the fixed background bounds. Choose R∗ > 0 small enough that all the balls lie in normal neighborhoods and (4.7) is at most ε. For all sufficiently small spatial dilations λ, and every 0 < δ ≤ 1 for which (4.10) holds, the mixed kernel extends to a neighborhood of {(x, y) : y ∈ Y, dγ(x, y) = rδ(y)}. The extension solves the two homogeneous equations and agrees with the prescribed lower cross and the fixed-separation continuation. It is smooth for each positive δ; no uniform norm as δ ↓ 0 is asserted here.
